open_questions.question: Australian legal wording is now sourced (fact_100-103, Marriage Act 1961 ss45-46 as reproduced on AustLII). Quote the s45(2) vow words and the s46(1) celebrant's words exactly as legal text, each with its fact marker, and link at the claim both the AustLII section page and the official Federal Register of Legislation page for the Act (https://www.legislation.gov.au/C2004A07402/latest/text). Quote the s46 text as the law states it, with no commentary. Personal vows: say the law requires these words 'or words to that effect' and that couples should ask their celebrant how their own vows fit around the legal ones; do not claim anything more. Ministers of religion may use their religious body's recognised form (s45(1)). For marrying overseas, the legal wording follows the country where you marry legally; New Zealand's rule (fact_02) may be cited with a link to our New Zealand guide. The 1 to 2 minute length is our advice; do not cite any search engine or AI summary.

facts.claim: As at November 2026, the Federal Register of Legislation lists the current compilation of the Marriage Act 1961 (No. 12, 1961) as C2026C00129, compilation 34, dated 28 March 2026, administered by the Attorney-General's Department; Part IV Division 2 includes section 45 'Form of ceremony' and section 46 'Certain authorised celebrants to explain nature of marriage relationship'.

[Copied from get-married-in-new-zealand 03-source-pack, same source and date.] Couples can write their own vows as long as each says words to the effect of 'I [name] take you [name] to be my legal wife/husband/partner'.

[Copied from get-married-in-new-zealand 03-source-pack, same source and date.] As at November 2026, govt.nz 'How to get married in NZ' states: most marriage ceremonies in New Zealand are personalised; you work with a celebrant to design the ceremony, you can hold it at any time, date and place you want, and you write your own vows.

[Copied from get-married-in-new-zealand 03-source-pack, same source and date.] As at November 2026, govt.nz 'How to get married in NZ' states: a registry ceremony has standard vows and must take place during business hours on a weekday (9am to 5pm, Monday to Friday), not on a public holiday.

[Copied from get-married-in-new-zealand 03-source-pack, same source and date.] As at November 2026, govt.nz 'Getting married' states: only registered celebrants can perform weddings or civil unions in New Zealand.

Marriage Act 1961 (Cth), as reproduced on AustLII (read 19 November 2026): s45(1): where a marriage is solemnised by an authorised celebrant who is a minister of religion, it may be solemnised according to any form and ceremony recognised as sufficient for the purpose by the religious body or organisation of which he or she is a minister.

Marriage Act 1961 (Cth), as reproduced on AustLII (read 19 November 2026): s45(2): where a marriage is solemnised by an authorised celebrant who is not a minister of religion, it is sufficient if each of the parties says to the other, in the presence of the authorised celebrant and the witnesses, the words: 'I call upon the persons here present to witness that I, A.B. (or C.D.), take thee, C.D. (or A.B.), to be my lawful wedded wife (or husband, or spouse)'; or words to that effect.

Marriage Act 1961 (Cth), as reproduced on AustLII (read 19 November 2026): s46(1): before a marriage is solemnised by an authorised celebrant who is not a minister of religion of a recognised denomination, the celebrant shall say to the parties, in the presence of the witnesses, the words: 'I am duly authorised by law to solemnise marriages according to law. Before you are joined in marriage in my presence and in the presence of these witnesses, I am to remind you of the solemn and binding nature of the relationship into which you are now about to enter. Marriage, according to law in Australia, is the union of 2 people to the exclusion of all others, voluntarily entered into for life.'; or words to that effect.

Marriage Act 1961 (Cth), as reproduced on AustLII (read 19 November 2026): s46(2): the Minister may exempt certain celebrants authorised under subsection 39(2) from s46(1) where satisfied their form of ceremony sufficiently states the nature and obligations of marriage.

insider_details.detail: Short personalised vows still need the legal core: in New Zealand each person must say words to the effect of 'I [name] take you [name] to be my legal wife/husband/partner', so build short vows around that line.

If you want short standard vows in New Zealand, a registry ceremony uses set vows but is limited to weekday business hours, which rarely suits a destination wedding day; most couples choose a personalised ceremony with a registered celebrant.

In Australia the ceremony form sits in s45 and the celebrant's explanation in s46 of the Marriage Act 1961 (current compilation 28 March 2026); confirm the exact legal words with your celebrant before writing short vows.
